To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the metabolic syndrome, as defined by the International Diabetes Foundation and National Cholesterol Education Program, predicts type 2 diabetes at least as well (and in some cases, better) than the World Health Organization's definition, despite not using oral glucose tolerance testing and without requiring the use of insulin resistance or microalbuminuric markers.
the metabolic syndrome predicts incident type 2 diabetes as well as the alternative criteria, and that modifications to the metabolic syndrome criteria do not improve predictive ability.

the International Diabetes Federation and National Cholesterol Education Program metabolic syndrome definitions predicted incident diabetes mellitus at least as well and in some cases better than the World Health Organization criteria, despite not requiring oral glucose tolerance testing and measures of insulin resistance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ability of the metabolic syndrome to predict diabetes.
the prediction of type 2 DM with alternative definitions of the metabolic syndrome.
the development of the metabolic syndrome, and its relationship with the development of diabetes and cardiovascular disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the International Diabetes Federation and the NCEP definitions of the metabolic syndrome were as effective as the WHO definition of the metabolic syndrome in predicting type 2 diabetes.
the NCEP definition of the metabolic syndrome is the best predictor of type 2 DM.
the NCEP definition of the metabolic syndrome is a useful tool to identify those at risk for diabetes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metabolic syndrome predicts type 2 diabetes, but it does not predict type 2 diabetes as well as type 2 diabetes.
, although the metabolic syndrome is a powerful predictor of DM, the NCEP definition is a reasonable choice for epidemiologic and clinical research.
, in the absence of a gold standard for metabolic syndrome, the NCEP definition, which is simple and easy to apply, is a reasonable choice for the prediction of DM in this population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metabolic syndrome is a powerful predictor of type 2 DM and that it is at least as powerful as the more expensive, time consuming and invasive tests of insulin sensitivity and glucose tolerance.

, despite not requiring oral glucose tolerance testing, measures of insulin resistance, or microalbumin, the metabolic syndrome definitions proposed by the International Diabetic Federation and the National Cholesterol Educational Program predict incident type 2 diabetes at least as well if not better than the World Health Organization criteria.
the NCEP definition of metabolic syndrome is at least as good as the WHO definition and better than the International Diabetes Federation definition in predicting type 2 diabetes.
